items.title: Georg Brunis Interview, 1958-06-03
items.q: [INTERVIEWER] Now, Monk Hazel still uses a... [INTERVIEWEE] Well, that's a French horn. Yeah, he uses the ground.

ctx.x: Well, Pansy Lane, that's Papa Lane's son. His name is Alfred. They called him Pansy. He played the trumpet and his brother-in-law, Leon Smello. I was playing the upright alto and he was playing the trombone. So he got under the weather one time and he didn't show up. And, uh, we were playing down at Crescent City Carnival Club. And, uh, Pansy says, uh, geez, what are we going to do for a trombone? He says, I said, well, I can play the trombone parts on the alto. He says, why don't you try the trombone, Bruno? So…
Now, Monk Hazel still uses a...
Well, that's a French horn. Yeah, he uses the ground. Well, it's an alto, but it's a French alto, a mellophone.
